steps.caption: Liquid LSD can be played from MIDI controllers, a Midi Fighter Twister, or OSC apps such as TouchOSC.
To put a knob on your controller, right-click it.
The ring pulses: it is waiting. Move a knob or fader on the controller and the two are linked.
Right-click again to stop waiting without linking anything.
Buttons learn the same way: right-click A, B, AUTO or TAP, then press a pad.
In Edit, right-click any slider for Learn MIDI and Learn OSC.
A Midi Fighter Twister needs no setup: plug it in and its 16 knobs are the 16 knobs on screen.
Its side button steps through the pages, like these tabs, and the screen follows.
Its rings show each knob's value, and on an FX row a push switches that slot off.
Preferences, under MIDI Controls, lists the pages. Each one is four rows.
Copy a page to a user file to change its rows and make it your own.
With MIDI on, this panel also shows incoming messages and every mapping, with its range, smoothing and soft takeover.
OSC Controls sets up control from a phone or tablet app such as TouchOSC.
Point the app at this computer and the inbound port. Feedback goes back on the outbound port.
Start Learn, then move a control in the app to link it. Right-clicking a slider does the same.
Mappings are saved in a profile, so each app or layout can have its own.
The Hardware page of the user guide covers each controller in detail.
